title: Request demuxing and link variance exploration
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploration notes for how request demuxing / request multiplexing strategies interact with cross-GPU link variance (NVLink/PCIe) and produce token-imbalance tail events. Goal is to capture microbench setups, preliminary findings, and next experiments to turn into a reproducible benchmark.

Context / why this matters:
- We see occasional per-request token-latency outliers in production where a single request stalls mid-generation while peers continue. Suspect interplay between host transfer scheduling, per-GPU work-stealing, and transient link congestion.
- Existing traces show two patterns: 1) uniform slowdowns across all GPUs (server-level), 2) single-token stalls affecting a subset of replicas. This doc targets the latter.

Quick glossary (how I use terms here):
- demuxing: router/unpacker step that splits an incoming batched payload into GPU subtasks (tensor/pipeline partitions).
- multiplexing: packing multiple independent requests into a single GPU batch.
- link variance: short-term changes in latency/bandwidth on NVLink or PCIe induced by competing DMA, asynchronous host copies, or microbursts.

Hypotheses:
1) Small transient PCIe read bursts from background metrics/telemetry cause per-GPU DMA queuing and a token stall for requests mapped to that GPU.
2) Demuxer placement (host vs. GPU) affects timing: host-side demux + large pinned-buffer transfers increases susceptibility to host scheduling jitter.
3) When multiplexing requests with heterogeneous sequence lengths, the short requests finishing earlier can cause imbalance signals that plus link jitter amplify tail latency.

Microbench designs executed so far (commands / setups):
- Baseline model: distilled-3B-like (fp16), 8-shard tensor-parallel (1 model replica across 8 GPUs), sequence len 1024, generation step 1-token loops.
- Controlled microburst generator: looped host->device cudaMemcpyAsync on a pinned buffer sized to emulate telemetry - run from a separate process. Varied sleep(0-3ms) between bursts.
- Demux modes: Host-demux (pre-CPU split + cudaMemcpyAll) vs GPU-demux (single packed tensor transferred, device kernel splits indices).
- Multiplexing mixes: even-length (all 1024) vs hetero-length mix (80% 16 tokens, 20% 1024).
- Per-token tracing: inserted lightweight tracepoints around prefetch, KV-cache read, NCCL op start/end, and device memcpy completion.

Measurements captured (representative):
- Baseline host-demux, no microburst: median per-token 6.3ms, p99 9.4ms.
- Host-demux + microburst (0.5ms bursts every 10ms): median 6.6ms, p99 18.2ms (observed isolated token stalls ~40-120ms).
- GPU-demux + microburst: median 6.4ms, p99 10.1ms (few stalls but much lower magnitude).
- Hetero multiplexing + host-demux + microburst: p99 > 200ms in some runs; stalls often align with large-request-to-small-request boundaries.

Observed traces / interesting signals:
- NCCL timings show an extra wait time on some ranks aligning with host-transfer completion events. The rank that stalls typically is waiting for a host->device memcpy to finish before invoking NCCL broadcast.
- Device kernels (demux-on-GPU) hide some of the DMA variance because only a single larger transfer happens and kernels defer demux until on-GPU, reducing host scheduling steps.
- When the microburst process used cudaMemcpyAsync with same stream as serving runtime (accidentally), we saw global stalls; using a separate stream localized the effect but did not eliminate it.

Immediate takeaways:
- Prefer GPU-side demux where feasible; it reduces small-host-transfer surface area and reduces single-rank dependency on timely host copy completion.
- Ensure background telemetry/metrics use throttled, low-priority streams and avoid large pinned-buffer synchronous copies during serving windows.
- Add instrumentation around host->device completion points and correlate with NCCL op start times for future incident triage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Repeat experiment with NVLink-only topology (no PCIe fallbacks) and with unified memory enabled to see if page faults cause similar stalls.
- Measure true PCIe bus contention when colocated noisy neighbors (other containers) perform frequent GPUDirect RDMA; simulate with a second process doing GPUDirect transfers.
- Evaluate impact of small-request packing policy: should we avoid packing short + long together? What heuristic yields best p99 under link jitter?
- Can we prefetch KV-cache pages earlier or overlap demux+transfer with previous token compute to mask jitter?

Next experiments (short plan):
1) NVLink-only cluster: repeat microburst injection and compare p99 distributions for host-demux vs gpu-demux. Track per-rank pci counters. (owner: Ethan)
2) Stream-priority isolation: run telemetry on low-prio stream and inject synthetic GPU memcpy on high-prio stream to see isolation boundaries. (owner: Priya)
3) Packing policy sweep: run synthetic workload with varying pack thresholds (min length for packing together) and compute cost vs p99 tradeoff. (owner: Marta)
4) Incident replay harness: automate microburst researcher harness (container + workload) and link to CI so PRs can't regress demux behavior. (owner: Joon)

Notes on reproducing locally:
- Use serve-dev-image:v2.3 (contains tracepoints). Start model with --demux=host or --demux=gpu.
- microburst tool: ./tools/microburst --size 2MB --interval 10ms --stream separate
- tracing: export TRACE_DIR=/tmp/traces; run collector: python tools/trace_collector.py --dir $TRACE_DIR

Rough remediation ideas for platform-level changes:
- Router-level: attach a demux-mode hint to model manifests; allow per-model enforcement of gpu-demux for models that expose many short-request mix.
- Runtime: detect suspicious host memcpy tail latencies and fall back to on-device demux path automatically for that batch.
- Scheduler: avoid tight co-location of heavy DMA telemetry agents with serving replicas; assign lower niceness to telemetry containers.

Loose thinking / fringe ideas:
- Stochastic demux: randomly choose a small fraction of requests to demux-on-gpu as canary to detect link variance early without full rollout.
- Adaptive packing: monitor per-rank lag metric; if a rank is lagging, temporarily avoid packing long requests with short ones for that batch.

References / tickets to follow up:
- SERV-4532: recurring p99 token stalls, prod incident 2024-08-11
- PR 1284: initial device-demux kernel + tests
- Confluence note: request demux design doc (link above)

Quick appendix (raw sample trace snippet):
- t=10234.123 r0: memcpy_cpu->gpu start (size 2MB)
- t=10234.128 r1: compute step finish
- t=10234.129 r0: memcpy_cpu->gpu done
- t=10234.130 rank3: NCCL allreduce start -> but rank3 waits 46ms before op due to lock on DMA queue
- t=10234.176 rank3: NCCL allreduce end -> rank3 token emitted at 10234.180 (others at 10234.132)

Status: draft — capturing early notes, experiments to be reproduced, will convert into a reproducible benchmark and a short post-mortem if patterns hold.

-- Priya
